questions.prompt: What does the remote name `origin` refer to?

options.text: A special protected branch on the server
The default name Git gives the remote you cloned from
The very first commit in the repository

questions.explanation: When you clone, Git names the source remote 'origin' by convention. It's an ordinary remote name — you can rename it or add others.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `git fetch` and `git pull`?

options.text: fetch uploads your commits; pull downloads them
fetch downloads without changing your branch; pull downloads and integrates into your branch
pull works offline; fetch needs a network

questions.explanation: fetch only updates remote-tracking branches like origin/main. pull does a fetch and then merges (or rebases) those changes into your current branch.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: git clone copies the repository's full history
git push uploads your local commits to a remote
git fetch merges remote changes into your current branch

questions.explanation: clone brings the full history, push uploads commits, and origin/main tracks the remote. fetch does NOT merge — that's what pull adds.

questions.prompt: To push a branch and set its upstream so later pushes need no arguments: git push -__ origin main
questions.explanation: git push -u origin main sets origin/main as the upstream (tracking) branch, so a bare git push/pull works afterward.

questions.prompt: Your `git push` is rejected as non-fast-forward because the remote has commits you don't have. What's the correct next step?

options.text: git push --force to overwrite the remote
Delete your branch and start over
git pull to integrate the remote's commits, then push again
Rename origin and push to the new name

questions.explanation: The rejection protects the remote's commits. Pull to merge/rebase them into your work (resolving any conflicts), then push. Force-pushing would erase the other commits.

questions.prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Fetch and integrate into your branch
Upload your commits to a remote

questions.explanation: clone creates the local copy, fetch downloads only, pull downloads and integrates, and push sends your commits upstream.
